Three ghost slots grow; the three REAL Blender 5.1.2 renders (crate, lantern, coin; pantry/ev_*_34.png) drop into them on their spoken names, one label each. Then an arrow draws to Godot's real app icon, small copies of the three assets ride it into the engine, and an ink check with one terracotta spark lands on 'the way you meant'.

B01.runner_up: Remotion LibraryIconRow (box / lantern / coin line icons)
B01.why: The act's cast is the three real assets; generic icons would teach nothing the renders don't, and the arrival into Godot's real icon is the second sentence's claim.

B04.visual_intent: Blender's icon + 'basic shapes'. Blender's five DEFAULT primitives (cube, cylinder, cone, UV sphere, plane), real renders from one camera so their sizes compare, land on their names. After the midpoint they give way to the lantern's five clay parts, spread out and oversized, which slide and shrink into place (move, scale, combine); the real coloured lantern fades over them on 'flat colour' ('5 shapes, flat colours'). Four prohibition marks land beside 'sculpting', 'painted textures', 'rigging', 'animation'.

B05.visual_intent: Two hero numbers land: '6' basic shapes, '500' triangles. A cube wireframe (hidden edges dashed) draws; one triangle of its top face fills terracotta ('a triangle'); then a diagonal cuts every face (hidden ones dashed): 'cube: 12 triangles'. A brace under the numbers: 'course limits', then 'not engine limits'.
B05.motion_claim: The diagonals cutting each face into two triangles is the definition; the brace re-labels the two numbers as course limits.
B05.runner_up: A real Blender render of the triangulated cube (like ev_sphere_default_vs_low.png)
